review.conclusion_reason: OPEN follows the project's fallback rule: the original contains substantive approval and a committee condition, but no qualifying ending or positive evidence of operation at the cutoff is established. Each clause has a named evidentiary gap. Formal status is supported only as 'no express ending found in reviewed materials,' not proof that none exists. The basis_rule field should identify the OPEN fallback rather than 'none'.
missed_evidence: EO 7252 paragraph 6 makes its termination effective January 1, 1936; its December 21, 1935 date is the issuance date. https://uscode.house.gov/us/usc/t15/s703/, lines 30–41.

EO 7252 paragraph 3 leaves the Consumers’ Division transfer without the paragraph 2 deadline; paragraph 5 modifies prior administrative orders only to the extent necessary. These provisions constrain the asserted general ending and do not expressly name EO 6271. Same source, lines 35–39.
review.stop_code_verdict: wrong (NOT_FOUND fits the first gap: qualifying order-specific ending evidence remains unlocated). The evidence slice identifies FIRST_END_UNPROVED and incomplete searches, not an owner-ruling requirement. The held draft rule assigns per-order judgment to the agent; its review status does not require owner permission. The project rules already classify unnamed general instruments as candidates only.
review.suspected_defect: Possible scope inflation in p8: a deadline for specified Commerce agencies is presented as ending all remaining NRA functions. Deliberate intent cannot be determined.

Title I authority appears verbatim; reading the complete held order confirms no express duration or termination provision.
Held original requires the committee and specifies five elected industry representatives and three appointed non-voting members.
Held original contains Roosevelt's printed signature and September 7, 1933 date.
The named type-rule file contains the quoted candidate date range and describes a per-order judgment; it supplies no established ending.

Govinfo link failed, but the same statutory note was directly read at https://uscode.house.gov/us/usc/t15/s703/, lines 30–32. It confirms the order date and termination language. Effective date was January 1, 1936, per paragraph 6.

Quotation is authentic but scope is overstated. Paragraph 2 imposes the April 1 deadline on the three agencies transferred to Commerce. Paragraph 3 separately transfers the Consumers’ Division to Labor without that deadline. Confirmed at https://uscode.house.gov/us/usc/t15/s703/, lines 33–36.
The named type-rule file expressly says it cannot establish an order's end, date, status or savings.
